verdict.rationale: Ardent lets developers test migrations and schema changes on isolated, production-identical Postgres branches, including per-PR branches in CI, before those changes reach production. That covers only the pre-validation half of the story: the evidence shows no mechanism for applying changes to production, such as merging a branch back, deploy requests, or online/non-locking DDL. missing for 10: merge-back or deploy-request workflow to production, online/non-blocking DDL to avoid table locks, schema diff/revert tooling, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can ship schema changes safely — online DDL, deploy requests, or branch-and-merge workflows — without locking or breaking production

citations.quote: Test migrations, run schema changes, and let coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor actually verify their database work — all against real data, without touching production.
Every PR runs against its own fresh database branch cloned from your connected source — no shared staging that drifts, no test runs corrupting each other
Ardent lets you run your full test suite, including destructive operations, against an exact copy of production.
